items.title: deskUnsloth: Levant reads files by line range, like cw
items.box:
Levant could not read any file bigger than one answer of his process (deskUnsloth.js is 88 KB; even a 13.8 KB test file was refused), so he could not read the code he was asked about. His file read is deskUnsloth's own file.load verb; no node verb changes.
Levant reads files with a tool that matches cw's: file.load takes an optional offset (the first line, from 1) and limit (how many lines).
Each answer carries the lines asked for, numbered, plus the file's total line count, so he knows how far he is and asks again for the next part.
A read that would not fit in one answer is cut at the last whole line that fits, and the answer says where it stopped.
A file small enough is still read whole when no range is given.
The tool's description tells the model to read a large file part by part.
Test: a file several answers long is read whole in parts, each answer under the cap, the lines numbered, the total line count given.
Ruling (andy, 2026-10-14): the tool-round limit (TOOL_ROUNDS = 3, deskUnsloth, from goal/G14.6) is tied to the context. If no context is specified, there is no limit either, like Unsloth Studio, which manages the context automatically.
